title: mimesis.score.v1
description: Timed score for one panel: three tracks (answer, reasoning, overlay) on one clock. Every time is absolute seconds from loop start. The renderer resolves state as a PURE FUNCTION of the current time -- it looks up what should be visible at t, it never accumulates elapsed time -- so a fifteen-minute loop cannot drift and a seek lands exactly. Produced by stage1/build_score.py.

loop_duration_s.description: Full cycle length. Renderer uses t = (clock_seconds % loop_duration_s).

source.description: audio.currentTime when narration is present. Both panels read the SAME clock object; there is no second timebase anywhere in the show.

fallback.description: With no audio file the renderer runs the identical lookup against a monotonic wall clock. No cue timing changes -- the score is authored so it is playable either way.

lead_offset_s.description: Seconds by which the reasoning track leads the answer track. Already applied to reasoning t_in values; recorded here so the offset can be re-derived after a retime. Negative means reasoning comes first, which is the intended direction.

answer.description: Large serif, bare wall beside the painting. Revealed character by character, blur to sharp.

t_out.description: When the block clears. Reading time, not reveal time.

char_onsets_ms.description: Onset of each character relative to t_in, one entry per character of text. PRECOMPUTED, not derived at render time from a cadence: this is what makes reveal a pure lookup and lets sentence-end pauses be retimed in JSON without touching code. Character i is at blur 6px/0.4 opacity at (t_in + onsets[i]) and fully resolved 120ms later.

claim_ids.description: Claims from claims.json covered by this block.

reasoning.description: Small monospace, on and around the painting, inside the surveillance layer. Hard appear, no blur, reduced opacity, faster than the answer. Mostly illegible at viewing distance by design.

line_interval_ms.description: Cadence between lines within this cue.

section.description: Matches an answer cue's section. This is the alignment that makes deliberation visibly precede output.

overlay.description: Surveillance layer cues, projected onto the oil. Every cue must name the Stage 1 datum it draws, via `source`. A cue with no source is invalid -- that is the rule that keeps decorative HUD elements out.

cue.description: Closed set. Adding a cue type means adding a Stage 1 measurement that backs it.

source.description: Provenance for this cue. `pointer` is a JSON Pointer into `file`.

fields.description: Which measured values the numerals print, by key path into the source record. The renderer formats them; it never composes a number of its own.

min_box_px.description: Suppress this cue when the face box renders smaller than this many projector pixels. Nested sub-boxes and brackets inside a 40px box are noise, not data; the score decides, not the renderer.
